slot.brief: A charged capacitor is connected to an uncharged one; ask the fraction of initial energy lost as heat using charge sharing.

stem: A $3\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor charged to $12$ V is connected in parallel to an uncharged $6\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor. What fraction of the initial energy is lost as heat?

verdicts.working: Initial charge is conserved: V_f=(3×12)/(3+6)=4 V. Thus U_i=½(3)(12²)=216 μJ and U_f=½(9)(4²)=72 μJ, so the fraction lost is (216−72)/216=2/3.

working:
$Q=C_1V$; $V_f=\dfrac{Q}{C_1+C_2}=\dfrac{C_1V}{C_1+C_2}$.
$\dfrac{U_f}{U_i}=\dfrac{C_1}{C_1+C_2}=\dfrac{1}{3}$; fraction lost $=1-\dfrac{1}{3}=\dfrac{2}{3}$

Independent check: Initial charge is conserved: V_f=(3×12)/(3+6)=4 V. Thus U_i=½(3)(12²)=216 μJ and U_f=½(9)(4²)=72 μJ, so the fraction lost is (216−72)/216=2/3.
solution:
Charge is conserved, so the final voltage is $V_f=\dfrac{C_1V}{C_1+C_2}=\dfrac{3\times12}{3+6}=4\,\text{V}$.
$$\frac{U_f}{U_i}=\frac{\frac12(C_1+C_2)V_f^2}{\frac12C_1V^2}=\frac{1}{3}$$
Hence, the fraction of initial energy lost as heat is $1-\dfrac{U_f}{U_i}=\boxed{\dfrac{2}{3}}$.
